Control data collection, tracking, and system services. Enable these features to enhance your privacy and security.
Control network access for apps. Based on GrapheneOS firewall implementation.

Implements a firewall-like system to control network access for individual apps. When enabled, apps must explicitly request network permissions, giving you granular control over which apps can access the internet.

Pros: Better privacy, prevents unauthorized data transmission, reduces data usage, blocks unwanted network access

Cons: Some apps may not work without network access, requires manual permission management

Visible Changes: You'll see network permission requests from apps. Apps without network permission won't be able to access the internet. Check network usage in Settings to see which apps are accessing the network.
Enhanced security features for apps. Improves memory allocator and address space protection.

App Hardening enhances the security of individual apps by improving memory protection mechanisms. This feature:

1. Memory Allocator Hardening: Uses hardened memory allocators (like Scudo or GWP-ASAN) that detect and prevent memory corruption attacks, buffer overflows, and use-after-free vulnerabilities.

2. Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR): Randomizes memory addresses to make it harder for attackers to predict memory locations and exploit vulnerabilities.

3. Stack Canaries: Adds protection values to detect stack buffer overflows before they can be exploited.

4. Enhanced Memory Isolation: Improves isolation between app processes and system processes.

How it works: When enabled, the system applies these security enhancements to all apps, making them more resistant to memory-based attacks and exploits. The hardening is transparent to apps but provides significant security improvements.

Pros: Better security against memory exploits, protection against buffer overflows, reduced risk of privilege escalation, enhanced app isolation

Cons: Slight performance overhead (typically 1-3%), slightly higher memory usage, some very old apps may have compatibility issues

Visible Changes: Apps will be more secure against memory-based attacks. You may notice a very slight performance impact (usually imperceptible). Security monitoring tools will show improved protection levels.
Control sensor access for apps to enhance privacy. Based on CalyxOS sensor blocking.

Provides granular control over which apps can access device sensors (accelerometer, gyroscope, magnetometer, etc.). When enabled, you can block sensor access for apps that don't need it.

Pros: Better privacy, prevents sensor-based tracking, reduces battery drain from sensor usage, more control over app permissions

Cons: Some apps may not function correctly without sensor access (games, fitness apps), requires manual permission management

Visible Changes: Apps will request sensor permissions. You can see which apps are using sensors in Settings > Apps > Permissions. Blocked apps won't be able to access sensors, improving privacy.
Enhanced location access control for better privacy protection.

Provides enhanced location access controls beyond standard Android permissions. Includes features like approximate location only, location access logging, and stricter permission enforcement.

Pros: Better location privacy, prevents precise tracking, more granular location control, access logging for transparency

Cons: Some location-based features may be less accurate, requires understanding of location permissions

Visible Changes: You'll have more options for location access (precise vs approximate). Location access will be logged and visible in settings. Apps requesting location will show enhanced permission dialogs.

Provides enhanced microphone access controls with features like access indicators, usage logging, and stricter permission enforcement. Shows when apps are accessing the microphone.

Pros: Better microphone privacy, prevents unauthorized audio recording, access indicators show when mic is in use, usage logging

Cons: Some voice-based apps may require manual permission grants, requires attention to permission requests

Visible Changes: You'll see indicators when the microphone is in use. Microphone access will be logged. Apps requesting microphone access will show enhanced permission dialogs with clear explanations.

Prevent system analytics and telemetry collection. When enabled, blocks all analytics services from collecting usage data, crash reports, and performance metrics. This helps protect your privacy by preventing data collection about how you use your device.

Prevent diagnostic and usage data collection. When enabled, stops the system from sending diagnostic information, error reports, and usage statistics to Google and other services. This includes crash reports and device health data.

Disable personalized recommendations and suggestions. When enabled, prevents the system from using your data to provide personalized content, app suggestions, and adaptive features. All recommendations will be generic and not based on your usage patterns.

Disable AI/ML features that may collect data. When enabled, blocks Android Intelligence services including smart suggestions, adaptive features, and machine learning-based optimizations. This prevents AI services from accessing your data for learning and personalization.

Prevent ad-related services and tracking. When enabled, blocks advertising ID services, ad personalization, and ad-related data collection. This prevents apps and services from tracking you for advertising purposes and using your advertising ID.

Prevent automatic cloud backup of device data. When enabled, stops automatic backup of your app data, settings, and device configuration to cloud services. Your data will remain only on your device. Note: Manual backups may still be possible.

Prevent system-level location services and tracking. When enabled, disables system-wide location services, preventing apps and services from accessing your location data. This includes GPS, network-based location, and location history. Apps requesting location will be denied access.

Prevent background network and Wi-Fi scanning. When enabled, stops the system from performing background Wi-Fi and Bluetooth scans to improve location accuracy and network discovery. This reduces battery usage and prevents passive location tracking through network scanning.

Prevent automatic WebView updates. When enabled, stops automatic updates to the Android System WebView component. This prevents the system from downloading and installing WebView updates, which may be used for security patches. Use with caution as this may leave your device vulnerable to web-based security issues.

Prevent automatic system and security updates. When enabled, blocks automatic download and installation of system updates, security patches, and OTA updates. This gives you full control over when to update, but may leave your device vulnerable to security issues. Manual updates may still be possible.

Prevent installation of apps from unknown sources. When enabled, blocks installation of apps from sources other than the Play Store or approved app stores. This prevents sideloading of APK files and installation from unknown sources, improving security but limiting app installation flexibility.

Enable various system optimizations to improve performance, battery life, and overall device responsiveness. Each optimization can be toggled independently.

These optimizations adjust system-level settings to enhance device performance. Changes take effect immediately and are persistent across reboots. Monitor your device performance after enabling optimizations.
View current optimization status and system information
Restrict background processes to improve performance and battery life • Shows running process count

Limits the number of background processes that can run simultaneously. When enabled, the system restricts background apps to 4 processes maximum, reducing RAM usage and improving battery life.

Pros: Better battery life, improved performance, less RAM usage, faster app switching

Cons: Background apps may close more frequently, delayed notifications from some apps, apps may need to restart more often

Visible Changes: You'll notice fewer apps running in the background, faster system response, and improved battery endurance. Check running apps in Developer Options to see the difference.
Optimize memory management for better performance

Enhances the Low Memory Killer (LMK) to be more aggressive in freeing up memory. This helps prevent memory-related slowdowns and keeps the system responsive.

Pros: Better multitasking, reduced lag, fewer out-of-memory errors, smoother performance

Cons: Apps may be killed more aggressively, some apps may restart when switching back

Visible Changes: You'll see more available RAM in system info, smoother app switching, and fewer system slowdowns. Monitor available memory in Settings > About phone to see improvements.
Set CPU governor to schedutil for balanced performance

Sets the CPU frequency governor to schedutil, which is the modern, efficient governor that balances performance and battery life. It dynamically adjusts CPU frequency based on workload.

Pros: Better battery life, responsive performance, automatic frequency scaling, modern kernel scheduler integration

Cons: Slightly less aggressive than performance mode, may not be optimal for extreme gaming

Visible Changes: You'll notice better battery life while maintaining smooth performance. CPU frequencies will scale more efficiently. Use CPU monitoring apps to see frequency changes.
Optimize I/O scheduler for better storage performance

Sets the I/O scheduler to mq-deadline, which is optimized for modern storage devices (eMMC, UFS, NVMe). It provides better read/write performance and lower latency.

Pros: Faster app loading, quicker file operations, better storage performance, reduced I/O wait times

Cons: Slightly higher CPU usage during I/O operations (negligible)

Visible Changes: Apps will load faster, file operations will be quicker, and overall storage performance improves. You'll notice faster app installs and smoother file browsing.
Enable and optimize ZRAM for better memory management

Enables ZRAM (compressed RAM) which uses a portion of RAM as compressed swap space. This effectively increases available memory without using slower storage.

Pros: More available memory, better multitasking, reduced app killing, improved performance on low-RAM devices

Cons: Slight CPU overhead for compression (minimal), may use more battery (negligible)

Visible Changes: You'll see more available memory, better multitasking capability, and fewer apps being killed. Check memory stats to see ZRAM usage and compressed memory benefits.
Optimize network usage to reduce power consumption • Shows current connection status

Optimizes network stack settings to reduce power consumption while maintaining connectivity. Adjusts network polling intervals and connection management.

Pros: Better battery life, reduced network-related wakeups, more efficient data usage

Cons: Slightly delayed network responses in some cases, may affect real-time apps

Visible Changes: You'll notice improved battery life, especially when using mobile data. Network-related battery drain will decrease. Monitor battery usage to see network optimization benefits. The summary shows your current network connection type (WiFi, Mobile, etc.).
Enable aggressive battery saving mode • Shows current battery level

Enables aggressive battery saving measures including reduced background activity, lower CPU frequencies, and optimized power management.

Pros: Significantly better battery life, reduced power consumption, longer device usage

Cons: Slightly reduced performance, delayed background sync, some features may be limited

Visible Changes: Battery will last noticeably longer. You'll see reduced battery drain in battery stats. Performance may be slightly reduced, but battery endurance improves significantly.
Optimize storage access patterns for better performance • Shows available storage

Optimizes storage I/O patterns, read-ahead settings, and caching strategies to improve storage performance and reduce fragmentation.

Pros: Faster file operations, quicker app loading, better storage performance, reduced storage fragmentation

Cons: Slightly more RAM usage for caching (minimal)

Visible Changes: File operations will be faster, apps will load quicker, and storage performance improves. You'll notice smoother file browsing and faster app installs.
Enable high performance mode for maximum speed

Enables maximum performance mode by setting CPU governor to performance, keeping CPU frequencies high for maximum speed.

Pros: Maximum performance, fastest app execution, best gaming performance, no CPU throttling

Cons: Significantly reduced battery life, increased heat generation, higher power consumption

Visible Changes: Device will run at maximum speed. You'll notice faster app launches, smoother gaming, but battery will drain much faster. Device may get warmer during use.
Monitor and control thermal throttling • Shows current thermal status

Controls how aggressively the system throttles performance when the device gets hot. When enabled, provides better thermal management to prevent overheating.

Pros: Better temperature management, prevents overheating, protects device hardware, more stable performance

Cons: May reduce performance when device is hot, CPU frequencies may be lowered during heavy use

Visible Changes: Device will manage temperature better. During heavy use, you may notice CPU frequencies being reduced to prevent overheating. Check thermal status in system info to monitor.
